title: NASA Mars facts — atmosphere and survival context
topics: survival habitat atmosphere air temperature pressure cold suit breathing weather
text: Mars has a thin atmosphere composed mainly of carbon dioxide, with nitrogen and argon. The atmosphere offers little protection from incoming space rocks and large temperature changes. Present-day surface liquid water is unstable under the thin atmosphere. These are planetary facts, not a weather report for any selected coordinate. A human habitat or EVA scenario requires engineered pressure, breathing support and thermal protection; this index does not specify certified equipment limits.
kind: NASA facts with explicitly labeled engineering implications

title: NASA SWIM — subsurface water ice
topics: water ice resources drinking fuel mining subsurface swim habitat
text: NASA's SWIM project combines mission observations to identify regions with evidence for subsurface water ice. Water ice and carbon dioxide ice are different resources. Water ice could support drinking water and propellant production after extraction and processing. A regional ice map does not establish a usable deposit or potable water at a particular point. Darkstar has not installed a spatial ice dataset and cannot determine ice abundance or depth at the selected location.
kind: NASA research summary; local availability unknown

title: NASA MOXIE — oxygen production demonstration
topics: oxygen atmosphere habitat breathing resources moxie isru exploration power
text: MOXIE demonstrated oxygen extraction from the Martian atmosphere aboard Perseverance. It tested a technology relevant to future breathing oxygen and rocket propellant. A demonstration is not a deployed astronaut life-support plant; a larger system and its storage, power and operational design are separate engineering work. It does not validate Darkstar's hypothetical oxygen consumption assumptions.
kind: NASA technology demonstration; engineering extrapolation requires validation

title: USGS SIM 3292 — global geological map
topics: geology rocks units map jezero exploration science resolution
text: Tanaka and colleagues' 2014 global geological map of Mars is USGS SIM 3292, published at 1:20,000,000 scale. It represents regional geological units and landforms inferred from remote sensing. It does not identify the composition or walking hazards of every outcrop. Darkstar's geology is separate from its numerical elevation datasets. A mapped geological unit is not evidence of traversability or a safe science stop.

title: NASA Jezero exploration science
topics: jezero lake delta sediment geology science exploration sample objective
text: Jezero was selected for Perseverance because its ancient lake and river-delta deposits provide a setting for investigating past environments and potential preservation of signs of ancient life. Past habitability is not proof of life. Feature-centre coordinates in Darkstar are regional destinations, not verified outcrops or rover sample locations.
kind: NASA exploration rationale; site access unverified

title: Darkstar terrain and Marswalk assumptions
topics: route mission marswalk eva rover energy oxygen power duration budget reserve slope elevation mola ctx assumptions
text: Darkstar computes routes with Python A* using numerical MOLA or regional CTX elevation. It cannot resolve hazards smaller than the source cells. Marswalk uses hypothetical constant walking speed and phase-specific oxygen and power rates, not NASA-certified astronaut performance. Emergency reserve is a configured fraction of capacity. Endpoint-to-cell connections are budgeted but not terrain-validated. Chat must report signed service outputs without recalculating mission totals. A route within configured budgets is not a safety clearance. Without an attached result, route and mission values are unavailable.
kind: Darkstar engineering assumptions, not NASA measurements
